The Sanskrit under 10.63.8 (ya īśire bhuvanasya pracetaso viśvasya sthātur jagataś ca mantavaḥ; te naḥ kṛtād akṛtād enasas pari adyā devāsaḥ pipṛtā svastaye) is Griffith’s 10.63.8 in day.js; the 10.61 verse-count shift does not reach 10.63. Sāyaṇa’s words found verbatim: kṛtāt kāyikāt pāpāt, akṛtāt kara-caraṇādibhir akṛtāt enasaḥ kiṃtu mānasāt pāpāc ca: committed sin as bodily, uncommitted as sin not done with hands, feet and the like but mental. The sentence carries exactly this; ‘no hand or foot’ is his kara-caraṇa. Webster’s bracketed note in Wilson reports the same of Sāyaṇa (‘from actual bodily sin and from mental sin’), so the reading is Sāyaṇa’s, not Webster’s own. Plain sense: 10.63 is to the Gods, with the All-Gods named at 10.63.6 and the Adityas throughout; ‘for happiness’ closes stanzas 5 and 7 to 14; ‘seeks release from wrongdoing’ reuses no four key words. Quoted key words ‘committed’, ‘uncommitted’ are within the limit. No school, no comparison, no softening. verse.js ok (Rig Veda 10.63.8, at [899,8]); entry-check.js ok on scratch/R-d113-p.json, no errors or warns.
